Run a pipeline of commands connected with pipes

Source: R/run_pipeline.R
run_pipeline.Rd

Runs commands connected with pipes, as cmd1 | cmd2 in a shell. The standard output of each command is the standard input of the next one. The data flows between the processes through operating system pipes, not through R. R gets the standard output of the last command and the standard error of every command.

Describe each command with run_step(), which takes the same command, arguments and env_name as run(). Each command can run in a different Conda environment. Commands that do not set an environment use the env_name of run_pipeline().

Usage

run_pipeline(
  ...,
  env_name = "condathis-env",
  method = "auto",
  verbose = c("output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner", "full"),
  error = c("cancel", "continue"),
  stdout = "|",
  stderr = "|",
  stdin = NULL,
  input = NULL,
  binary = FALSE,
  supervise = TRUE,
  cleanup_tree = TRUE,
  linux_pdeathsig = FALSE,
  activate = TRUE,
  timeout = Inf
)

Arguments

...

Two or more pipeline steps, built with run_step(), in pipeline order. Splice in a list of steps, built with list() or c(), with !!!, as in run_pipeline(!!!steps). c() on steps gives a list of steps that later c() calls extend, as in c(c(step_1, step_2), step_3). To add a step to a plain list or to NULL, wrap it in list(), as in c(steps, list(step)). c() with a plain list or NULL first splits a step into its fields. Any other value aborts with class condathis_run_pipeline_invalid_step, so name every option below in full. Fewer than two steps abort with class condathis_run_pipeline_too_few_commands.

env_name

Character string with the default environment of the steps that do not set their own, or an environment given by env_path(). Defaults to "condathis-env", which run_pipeline() creates (empty, with the backend that method selects) when it does not exist. run_pipeline() never creates any other missing environment and fails per error. A name must follow the rules of the env_name argument of run(). Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_env_name.

method

Character string naming the default backend of the steps that do not set their own method (see run_step()). "auto" (the default) uses the backend that owns each environment, and otherwise the first available backend in getOption("condathis.backend_priority") order (see condathis-options). Any name from list_registered_backend_names() selects that backend. "micromamba" is built in. The name of a backend whose package condathis knows also selects it, such as "rattler" of the rattlerthis package. condathis loads that package, and aborts with class condathis_backend_not_installed when it is not installed. "native" is a deprecated alias for "micromamba" (it warns once per session). If you name a backend other than the owner of an environment, condathis warns (condathis_backend_mismatch_warning) and uses the owner. An environment found under several backends aborts with class condathis_backend_ambiguous_env, unless method names one of them. With error = "continue", its steps get status 127. Steps that share an environment must agree on the backend. Otherwise run_pipeline() aborts with class condathis_run_pipeline_conflicting_method. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_method.

verbose

Character string that controls the console output. One of "output", "silent", "cmd", "spinner" and "full". Usage shows the default. "output" prints, while the pipeline runs, what it captures: the last command's standard output and every command's standard error, when their target is "|". "cmd" prints the whole pipeline first. "full" does both. "spinner" shows only a spinner, and "silent" shows nothing. TRUE means "output" and FALSE means "silent". Every level except "silent" shows a spinner in interactive sessions. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_verbose.

error

Character string that controls what happens when a command fails. With "cancel" (the default), run_pipeline() aborts:

  • a command that exits with a non-zero status: class condathis_run_pipeline_status_error (also condathis_status_error). A broken pipe can end a command that is not the last one: that does not count (see Broken pipes).

  • a timeout: class condathis_run_pipeline_timeout_error (also condathis_timeout_error).

  • a step environment that does not exist: class condathis_run_pipeline_env_not_found (also condathis_env_not_found). For an env_path(), the error also has condathis_env_path_not_found or condathis_env_path_not_conda_env.

  • a step environment found under several backends: class condathis_backend_ambiguous_env (see method).

  • a command that the backend fails to resolve, for example because an activate.d script of the environment fails: class condathis_run_pipeline_resolve_failed (also condathis_backend_error). The error keeps the condathis classes of the backend's error, for example condathis_micromamba_status_error, and has that error as its parent.

  • an invalid command description from a backend package (a bug in that package): class condathis_backend_resolve_run_invalid.

The status and timeout errors carry the fields status, stdout, stderr and timeout, as the errors of run() do. They also carry result (the condathis_pipeline object that error = "continue" returns) and statuses. With "continue", run_pipeline() returns the result instead. Every step in an environment that does not exist or is found under several backends gets status 127, with the reason in its stderr. So does every command that cannot be resolved or started. The other steps still run. A timeout gives status -9. Invalid values abort with class condathis_invalid_error. See condathis-conditions for all classes.

stdout

Standard output target of the last command: "|" (the default) captures it in the result, a file path writes it to that file, and NULL discards it. The standard output of every other command goes to the next command.

stderr

Standard error target for all processes. "|" (the default) captures each command's standard error in its result. A file path writes them all to that file, in command order once the pipeline finishes. NULL discards them. The stderr argument of run_step() replaces it for one command.

stdin

Standard input source of the first command: NULL (the default) for no input, the path of an existing file to read, or "|" to write input to it.

input

Character or raw vector written to the standard input of the first command, as in run(). Must be NULL (the default) unless stdin = "|". Other values abort with class condathis_invalid_input.

binary

Logical. Whether to return raw vectors, not UTF-8 text, for the standard error of every command and the standard output of the last one. Defaults to FALSE. It applies to the whole pipeline. There is no per-command setting.

supervise

Logical. Whether the processx supervisor watches each process: when the R session ends, even by a crash, the supervisor kills it. Defaults to TRUE, unlike in run() and run_bin(), since a pipeline starts several connected processes. Ignored on Windows, where supervised pipelines hang.

cleanup_tree

Logical. Whether to kill the process tree of each command, processes that it started in the background included. R kills the tree when it frees the process object of the command, at a garbage collection after the pipeline finishes. Defaults to TRUE, so that no command outlives the pipeline, unlike in run() and run_bin(), where a daemon that a command starts keeps running.

linux_pdeathsig

Logical. On Linux, whether each command gets SIGTERM when the R session ends, even by a crash. Ignored on other platforms. Defaults to FALSE.

activate

Logical. TRUE (the default) runs each command with the activation of its environment, as run() does. FALSE sets a fixed set of variables instead, without activate.d scripts (see condathis-options). Each command runs in the working directory of the R session, unless the activation of a backend gives another one.

timeout

Number of seconds the whole pipeline may take, the activations of the environments included: one deadline for all commands, not one per command. Defaults to Inf (no limit). run_pipeline() lowers a finite value above 2147483 (about 24.8 days) to that value. When the time is up, run_pipeline() kills every command still running (status -9 and timeout = TRUE in its result). It does not start a command whose activation took the rest of the time, and counts it as killed. error = "cancel" then aborts with class condathis_run_pipeline_timeout_error, and error = "continue" returns the result, with timeout = TRUE. Values that are not a single, non-negative number abort with class condathis_invalid_timeout.

Value

A condathis_pipeline object, invisibly, which prints as a short summary and which parse_output() reads. It is a classed list with:

status

Integer. The status of the pipeline: -9 when it timed out, otherwise the status of the first command that failed, or 0. A broken pipe can end a command that is not the last one: that does not count (see Broken pipes).

statuses

Integer vector, the exit status of each command. A command that a signal ends has the negative signal number, such as -13 for SIGPIPE.

processes

List of condathis_result objects, one per command, with the fields of a run() result: stdout is NA for every command but the last, env_name is the environment name or the directory of an env_path(), and timeout is TRUE for the commands that the timeout killed.

timeout

Logical. Whether the pipeline timed out.

cmd

Character string. The command lines of the commands, each part quoted, joined with " | ".

Broken pipes

A command that is not the last one ends as it would in a shell when it writes again after the next command has exited. On Linux and macOS, SIGPIPE kills it. Windows has no such signal. There, run_pipeline() reads the pipe in place of the command that exited. It kills the writer when more output comes after the pipe was empty for about one second in total. It also kills the writer when more than 64 KiB comes, which is what a Linux pipe holds. Output that was already in the pipe does not count. Either way, the status of the writer is -13, and that is not a failure. It does not make error = "cancel" abort, and it is not the status of the result. So seq 1 1000000 | head -n 1 has status 0. Programs that handle SIGPIPE themselves, such as R and Python, exit with their own status (R with 1, Python usually with 120), which counts as a failure. A command that writes nothing more keeps running, on every platform, and keeps its own status. On Windows, the reader that takes the place of the exited command is a small Rscript process. When it cannot start, the writer gets one second to exit on its own, and run_pipeline() then kills it.

See also

env_path() for an environment created outside condathis, and condathis-conditions for the condition classes.

Other commands: parse_output(), run(), run_bin(), run_step()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
condathis::with_sandbox_dir({
  # `pigz` and `ripgrep` (the `rg` binary) come from conda-forge, which
  # builds both for Linux, macOS and Windows. `rg` is used here instead
  # of GNU `grep`, which conda-forge has for Windows only as an MSYS2
  # package (with the "m2-" prefix).
  create_env("conda-forge::pigz", env_name = "pigz-env")
  create_env("conda-forge::ripgrep", env_name = "ripgrep-env")

  # Pipeline with per-command environments: count the reads of a FASTQ
  # file shipped with condathis. In this file, the header line of each
  # read starts with "@read".
  fastq_file <- fs::path_package(
    "condathis", "extdata", "sample1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz"
  )
  res <- run_pipeline(
    run_step(
      "pigz", "--decompress", "--stdout", fastq_file,
      env_name = "pigz-env"
    ),
    run_step("rg", "--count", "^@read", env_name = "ripgrep-env"),
    verbose = "silent"
  )
  print(parse_output(res))
  #> [1] "1086"

  # Steps are values: build a list of them, then splice it in with `!!!`
  steps <- list(
    run_step("rg", "--version", env_name = "ripgrep-env"),
    run_step("rg", "ripgrep", env_name = "ripgrep-env")
  )
  print(parse_output(run_pipeline(!!!steps, verbose = "silent")))
  #> [1] "ripgrep 15.2.0 (rev 78115297cd)"
})
} # }
